resources.string: Your iPhone. Your TV. Your sofa.
Keep Sofatap ready in the background after restarting the TV. Stop receiver pauses it until you start it or restart the TV.
The TV blocked background startup. Choose Start receiver, and check the TV’s app startup settings if this happens again.
Connect your iPhone and TV to the same home network, then start the receiver.
Connect to your home Wi-Fi or Ethernet, then stop and start the receiver.
Stop and start the receiver. If this continues, check the troubleshooting guide.
Using your TV remote, enable Sofatap in Accessibility settings. You can turn it off at any time.
Slide on your iPhone to move the pointer. Tap to activate a supported control; use two fingers to scroll.
This disconnects and forgets the previous iPhone. The new QR code expires in five minutes.
Scan with Sofatap on your iPhone
Start to show your pairing code
Could not display the pairing code
Use “Pair another iPhone” for a new code
Experimental pointer: clicks and scrolling depend on the TV app. Native remote keys and optional Sofatap keyboard are separate. Dragging and right-click remain unavailable.

Sofatap reads the current window’s control structure and draws a pointer so your paired iPhone can click and scroll at your direction. It does not read control text or perform autonomous tasks. Password and protected system screens are excluded. Enable this only if you want to control this TV, and disable it here at any time.
Wake and unlock the TV, then reconnect your iPhone. If control stays unavailable, restart Sofatap.
